# Color and brand

For any named brand, logo, brand kit or requested brand match, and for color contrast.

## Core

- Real brand facts win over inferred treatment. Use the selected snapshot's
  palette, type and supplied logo files, unmodified and in their documented
  variants.
- Exceptions are recorded, not improvised: they live in the brand snapshot's
  `overrides.md` or the active design direction.
- Say what was substituted or unavailable instead of claiming full brand
  fidelity, and name the kit used in the handoff.

## Using a kit

Read the project's brand snapshot (normally `brand/BRAND.md`, with `kit.json`
for tokens and the guides it links) as the `brand-kit` skill describes, and only
the fields the deliverable needs. Work for a website reads its site kit,
`brand/sites/<host>/kit.md`: take colours from `palette.json`, load the faces in
`fonts/` as local fonts, and place logos from `logos/` in the variant `kit.md`
marks transparent.

## Logos and marks

Inspect a logo file before placing it: pick the variant that suits the ground.
Verify a downloaded official mark against its published hash when one is given.
Partner and platform marks are sourced separately and never replace the user's
own brand as the design's identity.

## Color and contrast

A gradient word must stay readable at every stop; on
a dark ground, end on the lightest accent, never on dark purple, navy or black.

## After compression

Judge color in the encoded file, not the composition: faint decoration (glows,
patterns, watermark shapes) can vanish once encoded.

# Tool choice

For which tool builds the work and how to drive it: batch when mechanical, step when perceptual.

## Core

- **A tool the user names in this conversation wins.** Otherwise the
  `<voyager_creative_preferences>` block (a saved tool, or an app switched off)
  overrides everything below.
- **See what's available** in the `<voyager_environment>` block: its `Ready`
  and `Installed` lines list the apps on this machine. Outside the app (Claude
  Code, Codex), run `voyager capabilities --json`.
- **Parse JSON from stdout only.** Do not merge stderr with `2>&1` when parsing
  `--json` output; progress notices and live tool output go to stderr.
- **Defaults when the choice is yours** (the job is on Agent decides). Apps the
  user switched off remain unavailable.

  | Category              | Default                                                                                                                                  | Installed app: only when named, already in use, or its project file is asked for | Notes                                                                              |
  | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Motion                | Remotion, then HyperFrames                                                                                                               | After Effects                                                                    | Manim for equations                                                                |
  | Editing               | Voyager's video engine when ready, for transcript cuts, B-roll over speech, montages and ducked beds; FFmpeg via edit-video for the rest | Resolve, Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro                                             | Final Cut Pro gets an FCPXML handoff (edit-in-final-cut)                           |
  | Design & illustration | Voyager's design engine when ready, for static design; without it, HTML/CSS/SVG rendered headless, Python imaging                        | Illustrator, Photoshop                                                           | type and logos are authored                                                        |
  | 3D                    | Blender; without it, no 3D tool: say so in one line                                                                                      |                                                                                  |                                                                                    |
  | Slides                | Voyager's design engine when ready, exporting PPTX and PDF; without it python-pptx for PPTX, HTML rendered to PDF                        |                                                                                  | PPTX opens in Keynote, PowerPoint and Google Slides; check it in the installed one |
  | Music & audio         | ElevenLabs music and sound effects generated through `voyager`, mixed with FFmpeg                                                        |                                                                                  | voice cleanup with FFmpeg filters; Ableton Live and Logic Pro only when named      |

- **Another app's format wins:** when the input or requested output is another
  app's format (`.aep`, `.prproj`, `.drp`, `.ai`, `.psd`, `.als`, `.logicx`, and
  so on), work in that app and return the format the user gave.
- **Learn a third-party tool once.** For a substantial lookup that will recur,
  record essential commands, field names, sources and gotchas in a project note
  such as `notes/<tool>.md`, and read existing project notes before repeating the
  lookup. If project learning is available and allowed, save only a short summary
  and the notes path; leave long schemas in the file.
- **Batch when mechanical, step when perceptual.** Make one coherent edit
  between observations. Extend a settled design or cut through its mechanical
  repetitions together; pause when the next decision depends on what you see
  or hear.

## Asking for another app's name

"Make it in Keynote" or "a PowerPoint" names a tool, so it wins: drive
that app when it is installed, and change a native file they hand you in its
app. When it isn't installed, or they name Google Slides, build the PPTX with
python-pptx (PPTX for Keynote, PowerPoint and Google Slides import; PDF when
they only need to present or send it).

---
name: make-deck
description: "Slides and presentations; PPTX or PDF."
applications:
  - id: keynote
    role: primary
  - id: powerpoint
    role: alternative
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: optional
  craft: [tool-choice, color-and-brand]
---

When `<voyager_environment>` lists Voyager's design engine as ready, build the
deck there and export PPTX/PDF from it; otherwise build with python-pptx
(`uv run --no-project --with python-pptx python deck.py`; editable text, native
tables and charts, speaker notes), and make the PDF and
slide previews from it in the installed Keynote or PowerPoint, or LibreOffice.
With none installed, render the same slides as HTML at the slide size and
screenshot them headless (Chrome `--screenshot`) for the previews, and say the
PDF needs one of those apps or an HTML deck. A deck that only needs to be presented or sent may instead be HTML
slides printed to PDF (Chrome `--print-to-pdf`). Slides are 16:9 unless the
user asks otherwise.

## Deliver

| They said                    | Deliver                                                                 |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Keynote, PowerPoint, "pptx"  | `.pptx`                                                                 |
| Google Slides                | `.pptx`, and say: Drive, New, File upload, then Open with Google Slides |
| "send it", "present it", PDF | `.pdf`                                                                  |
| nothing                      | `.pptx` and `.pdf` both                                                 |

Font substitution, chart fidelity and wrapping can differ between apps: name any
fonts the recipient needs.

## Workflow

Its outline is the check-in that matters: get the argument approved first.

1. **Brief.** Audience, the decision or reaction you want, length (slides or
   minutes), presented live or read alone. A figure you need but don't have
   becomes a visible placeholder (`[ARR $X]`), never an invented one. A fictional
   company in the brief may get plausible made-up figures; say they are
   illustrative in the handoff.
   Use a project file as the subject's data only when it names the subject or
   the user points to it.
   Check `voyager direction resolve --json` and `brand/BRAND.md`. With neither,
   find a named company's kit with `voyager brand list --query COMPANY --json`
   and pull it per [brand-kit usage](../brand-kit/references/usage.md).
2. **Outline.** One line per slide: its type and its headline, written
   as the takeaway ("Churn halved after onboarding v2", not "Churn"). Read the
   headlines alone, in order: they should tell the whole story. Write the
   whole outline in your reply, as the last text before the approval question;
   the user never sees it in a file or your thinking.
   Choosing an app does not approve the outline.
   If no kit or direction exists and a company is named, offer to make a kit
   from its site in this same question.
   An answer Voyager chose automatically counts as approval; build without
   asking again.
3. **Direction.** Use the active [design direction](../brand-kit/references/directions.md)
   or brand kit first. With neither, pick one direction that fits the audience
   (editorial, Swiss, dark product or bold colour), name it in a line, and keep
   its palette and type consistent across the deck.
4. **Build** the title slide and the hardest content slide first. Inspect
   their previews and fix the system (grid, scale, colour) before the rest.
   Keep one editable deck with speaker notes on each slide and a repeatable
   source for revisions (the design document or python-pptx script).
   Revise that design document in place; don't fork it to a `_v2` copy.
5. **Hand off** with `voyager files present`: when built as a `.vdesign`,
   present it with `--deliverable "Deck"` and the `.pptx`/`.pdf`
   exports with `--deliverable none`. Otherwise present the exports with
   `--deliverable "Deck"` and the source with `--deliverable none`.
   Name the typefaces and anything illustrative or placeholder.

## The deck

- **Show, don't list.** Before writing bullets, ask whether this is a number, a
  comparison, a sequence or a picture, and use that slide type instead.
- **Speaker notes**, by default or on request, carry what you'd say: the talk
  track, the source of each number, and the transition to the next slide. A
  read-alone deck's notes carry the sources.
- The closing slide is the ask or the one thing to remember, never just
  "Thank you" or "Questions?".
- **Colour**: a background, an ink, one accent, and two supporting tones. The
  accent marks the one thing to look at; charts use it for the series that
  matters and grey for the rest.
